**The rail is a map of the document, and it holds live work only.** Every card sits beside the text it is about, the rail is as tall as the page rather than as tall as the window, and scrolling the prose scrolls the cards with it — so reaching a thread means scrolling to the text it is on, and nothing is clipped, folded or summarised as "+N more". One job: here is what needs you, beside the text it is about. Everything else has left it — settled conversations are a section of the review list (click the count in the bar to open it, at any width), a conversation whose text you deleted is in that list too, and the trail has no list at all. Hovering a card, or the words it is about, draws a hairline curve between them ending in a dot on the word; at rest there are no lines on the page, because that line answers "which words is this about" and the question only exists while it is being asked. (Until 2026-08-16 the rail was a fixed column with five mechanisms managing the overflow that guaranteed, and then four sections of which three were history. See `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-16-the-rail-scrolls.md` and `2026-08-16-the-rail-holds-live-work.md`.)
